description: Trigger evals for review-hard: it is the skeptical engineering-risk pass over finished code changes, unlike security-review (threat and ASVS focus), repo-consistency-sweep (known bug-class matching), api-contract-review (pre-build contract), or pr-feedback-ingest (turns existing review comments into a backlog).

should_trigger: sanity check my diff, anything that could bite us in prod?
Slice 03 is coded and the tests are green. Read the diff like a skeptic and tell me if anything is risky before I close it out.
I just finished the retry wrapper around the payment client in slice 02. Are there race conditions or swallowed errors in what I changed, and what is the smallest fix if so?
TASK_STATE.md says slices 01 to 04 are implemented. Before I package anything, review the whole change and tell me which files you actually looked at and what you skipped.
Run three independent passes over this branch's diff and keep only the findings they agree on.

should_not_trigger.prompt: Here is the draft OpenAPI spec for the new /invoices endpoints. Check the naming, pagination, and idempotency story before we write any handlers.
Slice 02 is implemented. Scan the changed files against our known defect classes for ordering bugs and convention drift, and skip anything I already declined last time.
The diff rewrites the login handler and token refresh. Do a threat model and an OWASP ASVS pass, and trace who can call what.
PR #212 has twelve comments from Greptile and two reviewers. Turn them into a backlog mapped to files and slices so I can fix them one by one.
I just wrote IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md. Critique it against the plan rubric and give me a revised draft with the weak slices fixed.
